title: Legacy (pre-OneAPI) authentication by product
aliases: zdx legacy oauth token key_secret sha256
when do I need the legacy api

prose.text: Each product's legacy API has its own credentials and token or session model. Whether a tenant is on the legacy path is a property of the tenant and the client, not of the product: [[zia.sdk-python.authentication:legacy-framework]].

prose.label: ZIA.
prose.text: The admin-plus-API-key session is in [[shared.legacy-api.zia-session]] and the external-IdP OAuth path in [[shared.legacy-api.zia-oauth]].

prose.label: ZPA.
prose.text: Signing in to the legacy ZPA API and its hosts are in [[zpa.api.authentication]] and [[zpa.api.base-paths:legacy-hosts]]. Whether the legacy ZPA portal allows several API keys per tenant is open {{gap:zpa-multiple-keys}}.

prose.label: Client Connector.
prose.text: The legacy login is [[zcc.api.authentication:legacy-login-request]], and its token travels in a header, not a cookie: [[zcc.api.authentication:legacy-auth-token-header]].

prose.label: Cloud & Branch Connector.
prose.text: {{cbc-prereqs}} {{cbc-session}} The session follows the same obfuscated-key login as legacy ZIA ([[shared.legacy-api.zia-session:create-session]]). {{cbc-activate-put}}

prose.label: ZDX.
prose.text: {{zdx-prereqs}} {{zdx-legacy-token}} {{zdx-signed-secret}} {{zdx-jwks-validate}} The two ZDX hosts and paths are discussed in [[doc:references/zdx/api.md]].

prose.label: Migration.
prose.text: Python SDK v2 drops the legacy clients: [[zia.sdk-python.authentication:v2-oneapi-only]]. Whether legacy credentials keep working after a tenant moves to ZIdentity is open {{gap:legacy-oneapi-coexistence}}.

checks.do: Which path the tenant and the client use (OneAPI through Authentication Service, or the product's legacy API), before choosing credentials.
For a ZDX legacy token request refused for its timestamp, whether the key_secret is SHA256 of secret:timestamp and the timestamp is within 15 minutes.
For a Cloud & Branch Connector legacy 401, whether the session sat idle for 30 minutes.

cbc-prereqs.statement: The legacy Cloud & Branch Connector API must be enabled for the organization by Zscaler Support, and needs an admin role with API Key Management permission and an API key.

quotes: You must enable the API for your organization. To enable the API, contact Zscaler Support or submit a Zscaler Support ticket.
You must have your Admin Role configured with API Key Management permission in the Zscaler Cloud & Branch Connector Admin Portal.
You must add an API key.

cbc-session.statement: A POST to /auth with an obfuscated API key, the admin's username and password, and a millisecond timestamp returns a `JSESSIONID` cookie, which by default expires 30 minutes after the session's last activity or at a DELETE to /auth; a later call returns 401.

quotes: To authenticate, send a POST request to the /auth endpoint with the following request body name-value pairs:
- apiKey: Obfuscated API key value.
- username: Username of the admin user that is provisioned.
A successful response to /auth returns a cookie in the Set-Cookie header, called JSESSIONID, that must be used in subsequent requests.
By default, the JSESSIONID expires within 30 minutes from the last activity or request on that session, or when you explicitly log out by sending a DELETE request to /auth.
If API calls are made after the expiry of JSESSIONID, a 401 Unauthorized error is returned.
- password: Password of the admin user.
- timestamp: Long value that represents the current time in milliseconds since midnight, January 1, 1970 UTC.

cbc-activate-put.statement: Legacy Cloud & Branch Connector changes are activated with a PUT to /ecAdminActivateStatus/activate.

quotes: After modifying any configurations, you must activate the changes by sending a PUT request to /ecAdminActivateStatus/activate.

zdx-prereqs.statement: The legacy ZDX API needs an API key (key ID and key secret) and the ZDX Advanced Plan; a bearer token lasts 3,600 seconds.

quotes: Be a ZDX Advanced Plan User.
The API key includes an API Key ID and API Key Secret that are required to access the ZDX API and to create a bearer access token.
Upon successful authentication, a bearer token will last 3,600 seconds or 60 minutes.

zdx-legacy-token.statement: The legacy ZDX reference posts `key_id` and `key_secret` to /oauth/token on the production server `https://api.zdxcloud.net/v1` and returns a token valid for 3600 seconds.

expect.description: Successful Operation. The response contains the token and the token type. The token is valid for 3600 seconds.

zdx-signed-secret.statement: The OneAPI ZDX contract's /v1/oauth/token takes `key_secret` as SHA256 of the secret key and timestamp (`SHA256('secret key:timestamp')`) and a `timestamp` in epoch seconds, and requests sent after 15 minutes are invalid.

key_secret.description: The secret key. This must be SHA256 for secret key and timestamp. For example, SHA256('secret key:timestamp').

timestamp.description: The time stamp in epoch seconds. Requests sent after 15 mins are invalid.

zdx-jwks-validate.statement: The ZDX auth reference also has GET /oauth/jwks, returning the public keys that verify the JWT tokens, and GET /oauth/validate, which checks whether the token is valid.

expect.description: Returns a JSON Web Key Set (JWKS) that contains the public keys that can be used to verify the JWT tokens.
Checks if the JWT token is valid.

wa-token.statement: Workflow Automation's API is enabled with its subscription; a POST of `key_id` and `key_secret` to /v1/auth/api-key/token on `https://api.us1.zsworkflow.net` returns 201 with a bearer token and its `expires_in` (43200 in the example), and a call after the token expires returns 401.

quotes: The API management is automatically enabled if you have a subscription to Workflow Automation.
The base URL for the API is https://api.us1.zsworkflow.net.
{ "expires_in":43200, "token_type":"Bearer",
If API calls are made after the expiry of the authorization token, a 401 error is returned.

expect.description: Successful operation. A new authorization token is created.

wa-key-expiry.statement: A Workflow Automation API key expires only when its Expire after option is enabled, and its key secret is visible only when the key is first created.

quotes: The API key is only valid for a set number of days if the Expire after time option is enabled in the Workflow Automation Admin Portal. If not, the authentication key does not expire.
The key secret is only accessible within the Workflow Automation Admin Portal when the API key is created for the first time.

wa-errors.statement: A failed Workflow Automation token request returns 401 when the API key is expired or disabled and 500 when the request is corrupt.

quotes: the response code returns a 401 error if the API key is expired or disabled and a 500 error if the request is corrupt.

legacy-oneapi-coexistence.title: Whether legacy credentials keep working after a tenant migrates to ZIdentity
legacy-oneapi-coexistence.detail: Unverified legacy statement: migration to ZIdentity is opt-in and some tenants stay on legacy auth indefinitely; after a tenant migrates, its legacy keys keep working in parallel for a transition period, so legacy and OneAPI can coexist on one tenant and a script on stale legacy credentials can still succeed. No captured source states the migration terms or how long legacy credentials remain valid.
legacy-oneapi-coexistence.blocks: telling an operator whether a migrated tenant's legacy API keys are still live

zpa-multiple-keys.title: Whether a ZPA tenant can hold several legacy API keys
zpa-multiple-keys.detail: Unverified legacy statement: legacy ZPA API keys are managed in the ZPA portal and a tenant can have multiple keys (unlike ZIA's single cloud service API key). The captured ZPA getting-started page says only that admins with full API Key Management access create keys; no captured page states a count.
zpa-multiple-keys.blocks: planning one key per script on a legacy ZPA tenant
